noteRef.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specPoints.text: understand the general structure of the circulation system, including the blood vessels to and from the heart and lungs, liver and kidneys

primer.text: Your blood travels a one-way loop through a closed network of vessels, stopping at the lungs to collect oxygen and at the liver and kidneys to deliver and collect. This note maps the whole circuit and the named vessels that feed each organ, including the two famous exceptions.

lessons.title: The Circulation and Its Named Vessels
sourceHeadings: Main Blood Vessels of the Circulatory System Table
lessons.opening: Blood flows one way around a closed network: arteries carry it outward from the heart, capillaries trade with the organs, and veins gather it back, with the pulmonary pair forming the famous exception pair.
keyPoints: Arteries usually carry oxygenated blood away from the heart.
The pulmonary artery is the exception, taking deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
The pulmonary vein returns freshly oxygenated blood, the reverse exception.
Arteries narrow into arterioles, then capillaries, then widen into venules and veins.
Lymphatic vessels return leaked tissue fluid to the circulation.

low.restatement: Outward arteries, returning veins, one-way flow, and the pulmonary pair breaking the oxygen rule.
low.analogy: A delivery van loop: outbound on the motorway, doorstep stops, then the return lane home.
low.examPointer: Learn the vessel table: vena cava and pulmonary vein in; aorta and pulmonary artery out.

medium.restatement: Each organ has its own in-pair and out-pair — hepatic artery plus portal vein for the liver, renal artery and vein for the kidneys — all wired into the one-way loop.
medium.analogy: A ring road with private driveways: every house (organ) has its own entrance and exit onto the same circuit.
medium.examPointer: Practise writing the liver row in full: hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein toward it, hepatic vein away.

check.stem: Which vessels carry blood away from the heart?

options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Veins return blood toward the heart.
Venules collect blood between capillaries and veins.
They return tissue fluid, pumping no blood from the heart.

check.stem: Which vessel breaks the rule that arteries carry oxygenated blood?

options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
The aorta carries oxygenated blood outward.
It carries oxygenated blood to the kidneys.
It is a vein, not an artery.

check.stem: Which pair of vessels connects toward the liver?

options.text: The hepatic artery and the hepatic portal vein
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
The portal vein also runs toward it, carrying digested food.
The hepatic vein carries blood away from the liver.
Those belong to the kidneys.

check.stem: What sequence describes the narrowing and widening between heart and organ?

options.text: Artery to arteriole to capillary to venule to vein
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: Artery to venule to capillary to vein
options.explanation: Arterioles come before capillaries, not venules.
That reverses the one-way loop.
Arteries branch into arterioles, not the reverse.

check.stem: What role do the lymphatic vessels play alongside the blood circulation?

options.text: They collect excess tissue fluid and return it to the circulatory system
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: They carry oxygen to the lungs
options.explanation: The pulmonary vessels do that.

options.text: They pump blood faster than arteries
options.explanation: They carry fluid, not blood, and without a pump.

options.text: They remove blood from the body
options.explanation: Nothing removes blood; the loop is closed.

check.stem: Name the vessels bringing blood toward the heart and toward the lungs.
check.modelAnswer: The vena cava and pulmonary vein bring blood toward the heart, and the pulmonary artery carries it toward the lungs.

check.stem: State which vessel carries blood away from the kidneys.
check.modelAnswer: The renal vein carries blood away from the kidneys.

check.stem: Explain why the pulmonary vessels are called the exception pair.
check.modelAnswer: Because each breaks its family's oxygen rule: the artery carries deoxygenated blood and the vein carries oxygenated blood, opposite to every other vessel of its kind.

check.stem: A diagram labels four vessels at the liver but mixes two from the kidneys. Identify the liver set.
check.modelAnswer: The liver set is the hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein toward it with the hepatic vein away; the renal artery and vein belong to the kidneys.

glossary.definition: The artery carrying deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
The vein bringing oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
The vein carrying digested food from the gut toward the liver.
Drainage vessels returning leaked tissue fluid to the circulation.

figures.alt: Diagram of the circulatory system showing blood flow between the heart, lungs, liver, gut, kidneys, and other organs with labelled veins and arteries.
